concurrency_mechanism: one worker process; activity_executor=concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=20); max_concurrent_activities=20. time.sleep(0.1) releases the GIL, so 20 threads serve 20 activities at once. Activity task pollers left at the SDK default PollerBehaviorSimpleMaximum(5).
notes: Temporal 1.29.7, Postgres variant of the official docker-compose (numHistoryShards 4), on an otherwise idle m7i.8xlarge (32 vCPU / 16 physical cores). Config: dynamicconfig/development-sql.yaml exactly as published by temporalio/docker-compose; history.transferProcessorMaxPollRPS left at its default of 20. Workload: 2000 independent activities per rep, organised as 100 workflows each fanning out 20 activities onto a dedicated activity task queue (bench-act); the workflow worker runs in a separate process on bench-wf so workflow tasks never take activity slots. All 2000 activity tasks are enqueued and waiting before the activity worker is released (verified per rep: 2000/2000 ActivityTaskScheduled before release, plus a 5 s idle settle; raising that settle to 30 s moved throughput by 1%, so submission is outside the measured window). 6 reps, rep 0 discarded as warmup. Every number is derived from the server's event history (ActivityTaskScheduled / Started / Completed), not from harness wall clock. span_s = last completion - first start; throughput = 2000 / span. latency_p50_s and latency_p95_s are scheduled -> completed and are therefore dominated by the pre-enqueued backlog wait, not by Temporal's dispatch latency. exec_p50_s is started -> completed and includes the completion round trip to the server. Measured ceiling for this workload with the same worker code and no orchestrator in the path: 199.2 activities/s; median here is 112.5/s, 56% of that ceiling. Peak concurrency derived from timestamps never exceeded 20 in any rep.
